summary: Baseline documentation of the existing codebase, after completing the agentic phase
changes: Documented the project: sixteen existing features, the blackboard architecture, setup and configuration, and the full git history since the project started on 2026-06-23
Added read-only tools — read a file, list a directory, search the code, plus web search — to seven agents through a single can_look flag
Added a write–test–fix loop to the Coder: it writes files, runs the project's own test suite, reads the failure and corrects it inside one stage
Confined writing to the paths the approved file plan named, and made run_tests take no command so it cannot become a general shell
Added plan editing in the browser, which clears the approval so an edited plan must be read again (SDLC-5)
Added a check refusing a plan that names a file which does not exist, re-asking once before refusing the run (SDLC-6)
Fixed the Architect being told to add a Dockerfile and README on every run — inside a repository the file plan is now a diff, not an inventory
Fixed to_pdf reporting success when it had rendered nothing (SDLC-ISSUE-1)
Rewrote the status and roadmap papers to describe what exists rather than what was proposed
problems: Every significant failure in live use came from agents being unable to open a file, not from poor prompting — a build system invented because Gradle could not be seen, a file planned because a directory could not be listed
A live run revealed the Architect was being instructed to include a Dockerfile and README on every run, so a request to restyle one screen planned ten files
A correct no-op was failing runs: given an already-passing file the Coder changed nothing, and the code reported that as producing nothing
Regenerating the two papers appeared to work and did nothing, because the PDF renderer only checked that the output file existed
solutions: Two tiers of tooling: reading is available to any agent that opts in and can change nothing; writing and running tests belong to the Coder alone and are confined to the approved plan
Inside a repository the file plan is now stated to be a diff rather than an inventory, in both the prompt file and the user turn
A no-op backed by a green test suite is accepted as a result; nothing written with a red suite still fails the run
The renderer compares modification times and resolves the output path, with tests covering both
nextSteps: Decide whether the Coder should be allowed to run a linter and a build behind an allowlist (SDLC-17)
Run a milestone build against the live API — the largest untested surface in the factory (SDLC-18)
Add an Android emulator and a macOS runner so mobile work can verify itself (SDLC-19)
Update README.md, which still describes six agents (SDLC-ISSUE-3)
